Subject: Post-demo: Model fit & benchmarks for Acme Retail

Hi Lucas & Priya,

Thanks again for your time today — it was great to walk through a quick demo and hear more about Acme's customer support use cases (short replies, routing hints, and soft retrieval for product FAQs).

As promised, I'm sharing the items we discussed and next steps:

- Recommended models for initial eval: Open models (gptj-6B-quant, Llama-3-13B-8bit) for conversational latency/cost balance; Redwood-verified gpt-lite-13b for higher throughput with similar quality in our tests.
- Benchmark snapshot & perf profiles: https://redwood.ai/benchmarks/acme-retail-20260301 (includes TPS, p50/p95/p99 latencies for each model/instance type)
- Prompt set: attached acme_prompt_set_v1.csv (examples pulled from your support transcripts)
- Follow-ups: 1) Can you confirm expected concurrent users for the pilot? 2) If acceptable, we propose a 2-week POC on Dedicated with a small reserved pool.

I've attached the prompt set and a one-page PDF with Redwood-verified performance profiles for the three recommended model configurations.

Next meeting: I'd like to schedule a 30-min technical sync with your infra/security and our SE to scope data handling and quantization options — are you available next Wednesday?

Thanks,

Vanessa Ortiz

vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com

Thanks Vanessa — good stuff. A couple quick clarifications:

- Our initial pilot will likely see ~150 concurrent support agents (estimate ~3k messages/min at peak). Can you confirm the TPS numbers we should expect and what instance sizes you recommend for p95 < 300ms?
- You mentioned 'Redwood-verified' profiles — are those measured conversational (with KV cache) or single-turn? We care about end-to-end latencies including routing overhead.

Also, curious on quality regression detection — how do you surface regressions when swapping model/quantization profiles?

Best,
Lucas
Head of Support Automation
Lucas.Cheng@acmeretail.com

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Lucas Cheng <lucas.cheng@acmeretail.com>, Priya Rao <priya.rao@acmeretail.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-03T11:25:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Model fit & benchmarks for Acme Retail

Hi Lucas — great questions. Short answers + I'll let Marissa add the technical numbers below.

- TPS/instance: For the workload you described (~3k messages/min peak -> ~50 TPS sustained), our recommendation for p95 < 300ms is:
  * Llama-3-13B-8bit on m60-1 (single GPU) achieves ~60-80 TPS with p95 ~210ms (conversational, KV cache enabled)
  * gpt-lite-13b (int8 optimized) on m60-1 achieves ~90-110 TPS with p95 ~250ms
  * For headroom and redundancy, Dedicated pool with 2 GPUs (autoscale policy) is typical.
- Profiles linked: https://redwood.ai/benchmarks/acme-retail-20260301 — those are conversational measurements (50 token average response) including KV cache; they include end-to-end injection points (routing + runtime). See p50/p95/p99 breakdowns.
- Quality regression detection: Redwood Optimize hooks eval sets (we can run your prompt set) and produce per-prompt quality deltas; regressions flagged on threshold (e.g., >3% BLEU/ROUGE or manual labeling delta). We also surface prompt-level failure rates and semantic similarity drift alerts.

Attached: acme_prompt_set_v1.csv (updated with a 'priority' column) and the one-pager benchmark PDF.

If acceptable, I'll loop in Rishi (pricing) and Dev (security/infra) for the POC scoping call. Suggested times next Wed: 10:00 or 15:00 PT.

Thanks,
Vanessa

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Lucas Cheng <lucas.cheng@acmeretail.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-04T14:00:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Model fit & benchmarks for Acme Retail

Hi all — added more detail on the benchmark numbers and operational knobs. Quick table (excerpt):

- gpt-lite-13b (int8, optimized kernels) on m60-1: throughput 95 TPS, p50=85ms, p95=250ms, p99=420ms
- Llama-3-13B-8bit on m60-1: throughput 70 TPS, p50=75ms, p95=210ms, p99=360ms
- gptj-6B-quant on m40-1: throughput 40 TPS, p50=110ms, p95=420ms

Notes:
- All numbers are measured with our conversational harness (50 token responses) and include runtime routing overhead.
- Quantized variants reduce memory and cost but can shift subtle generation behavior; we recommend running your prompt set (attached) through our eval harness to compare semantic fidelity before rollout.
- Fallback strategy: recommended canary + automatic fallback to a higher-precision variant if regression > threshold for key intent prompts.

Links:
- Detailed perf + raw traces: https://redwood.ai/benchmarks/acme-retail-20260301
- Eval job (runs on your prompt set): https://drive.google.com/open?id=1A2B3Cacme_prompt_set
- HubSpot deal: https://hubspot.com/deal/DEAL-2026-045

Next step: if you confirm the pilot sizing (2x m60-1 for Dedicated with canary) we'll prepare a scoped MSA + pilot quote. Dev — could you confirm the default data retention/audit log package we should propose for Acme?

—Marissa
Senior SE | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
